answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying identity to non-transferable, slowly accruing reputation: each agent must forge its standing through sustained, costly work rather than cheap signup. Like quartz that crystallizes gradually and cannot be faked cheaply, trust should accumulate over time and be soulbound, so an attacker spinning up a thousand ivory-tower aliases gains nothing — every new identity starts at zero and must pay the full price of history before it can trade.
